title: Ackless tiling + reassembly policy for SSE streams to improve reconnect determinism and tool-call integrity
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Problem: our current SSE streaming implementation assumes explicit per-chunk acks or resume tokens for reliable reconnects. This has led to edge cases with function/tool calls and structured output where duplicated or missing partial frames produce inconsistent tool invocations and downstream side-effects (webhooks, DB writes).

Goal: implement an 'ackless tiling and reassembly' policy that allows clients to resume streams deterministically without a per-chunk ack roundtrip while preserving idempotence for function/tool calls and structured outputs. The policy should: (1) tile output into deterministic segment IDs derived from stable granularity (prefix-length+message-hash), (2) carry minimal provenance metadata so reconnects can reconcile which tiles were already consumed, and (3) enforce a server-side replay-suppression mechanism for tool calls and external side-effects.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Clients reconnecting with last_seen_tile_id resume from the next unseen tile in >= 99.9% of cases in local tests. 2) No duplicate tool call side-effects observed during a controlled chaos test (simulated network partitions). 3) End-to-end latency impact <= 5% at p95 when tiling enabled. 4) New protocol documented and SDK changes implemented for JS and Python. 5) Integration tests added that validate structured JSON chunk boundaries against function call integrity.
implementation_notes:
High-level approach: create deterministic tile ids by combining (model_epoch, output_prefix_hash, token_window_index, frame_seq) and encode as a compact base62 token. Tiles are transmitted as SSE events of type 'tile' with fields: id, seq, partial, checksum, provenance. Server maintains short-lived checkpoint map per session (LRU, TTL 60s) to track last emitted tile id; on reconnect client supplies last_seen_tile_id in header X-RW-Last-Tile. Server computes delta and begins streaming subsequent tiles. For tool calls: tile metadata includes tool_call_marker and a call_id derived from content hash + model_epoch; server verifies call_id against a persistent de-dup store (write-ahead log) before invoking backends. The de-dup store is sharded and has eventual eviction policy for non-idempotent calls longer than 24h.

Tradeoffs considered: full per-chunk acks (higher reliability) vs. ackless tiling (lower latency, fewer RTTs). We accept small window of potential duplicate frames for non-critical outputs but enforce strict dedup for tool calls. We considered resume tokens (opaque blobs) but those complicate interoperability with older SDKs; tile ids are human-decodable and can be validated by proxies.
api_changes:
- SSE event type 'tile' with payload schema stringified JSON; example: event: tile
data: {"id":"t_abc123", "seq":42, "partial":true, "checksum":"sha256:...", "proto":{...}}

- New request header: X-RW-Last-Tile: t_abc123
- New error: 409 TILE_MISMATCH when client's last_seen cannot be reconciled (requires full stream reset)
- SDKs: add Stream.resume(lastTileId) helper and automatic header injection.
testing_plan: Unit: tile id generation fuzz tests, checksum mismatch handling, call_id uniqueness. Integration: end-to-end with JS SDK harness, simulate network partitions and client retries. Chaos: run 24h mixed load test with randomized connection drops, assert no more than 1 duplicate tool call per 1M calls. Load: measure p95 latency with and without tiling at target QPS 5k single-region. Observability: add metrics rw.stream.tiles_emitted, rw.stream.resume_success_rate, rw.stream.duplicate_tool_calls.
rollout_plan: 1) Merge feature flag behind 'ackless-tiling' (canary fraction 1%). 2) Canaries in dev and staging clusters; validate integration tests and metrics for 48h. 3) Incrementally enable for 5%/25%/75%/100% over 3-5 days while monitoring resume_success_rate and duplicate_tool_calls. 4) If duplicate_tool_calls > 0.0001% or resume_success_rate < 99.5% pause rollout and revert flag. 5) Post-release: run 7d retrospective and include runtime metrics in console dashboard.

comments: 2026-03-02 - Maya Chen: initial ticket created after incident where a webhook receiver executed duplicate payments during a reconnect. Logging showed no resume token present.
2026-03-04 - Arjun Patel (review): prefer call_id derivation to be canonicalized JSON hash to avoid whitespace canonicalization issues; added to implementation notes.

2026-03-06 - Design review notes: decided on 60s TTL for checkpoint map to balance memory use vs typical client reconnect windows; to revisit after telemetry. Action: add metric for checkpoint_map_size.
2026-03-08 - PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/2897 - initial tile encoder + server-side handler. Tests failing in dedup path; investigating shard locking semantics.

2026-03-10 - QA: integration harness shows resume success 99.92% (good) but observed 2 duplicate tool calls across 500k calls during chaos test; root cause: race on dedup-store replication lag for cross-region failover. Next: introduce local in-memory hedged-confirmation for non-idempotent calls and escalate to infra for dedup-store consistency tuning.
notes_for_reviewer: Focus on dedup-store semantics and potential performance impact of call_id lookup on hot paths. Pay attention to memory sizing of session checkpoint maps (default TTL 60s) and shard count. Security: ensure call_id derivation uses HMAC with service key before persisting to avoid leaking payload hashes in logs.
follow_up_tasks: postmortem: document incident and mitigation steps
optimize: replace base62 mapping with compact varint encoding if tile id growth affects payload size
sdk: add declarative opt-out flag for customers that prefer per-chunk acking
